currentContext.business: The Company's business comprises real estate development for housing projects in and around Pune, wind power generation and investment activities. Real estate development is carried out through its subsidiaries, namely AMJ Land Developers (a firm in which the Company holds 95% stake) and wholly owned subsidiary AMJ Realty Ltd; its flagship is the gated residential project 'GREENS', which currently houses 722 families in 7 residential towers with an 8th tower under construction, while the 'GREEN VILLE' project remains on hold. Wind power is generated from three wind mills of an aggregate capacity of 4.6 MW in Maharashtra and sold to industrial consumers under the Open Access system, and part of the Company's land and buildings at Thergaon, Pune is leased to Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd under a Leave & License Agreement.

Real estate development (housing): GREENS - self-contained prestigious gated residential project, Pune (7 towers handed over; 8th tower of 2, 3 and 4 BHK apartments under construction)
GREEN VILLE - project currently on hold
Redevelopment of existing old housing schemes (pursued through AMJ Realty Ltd; two redevelopment projects awarded, due diligence and documentation in progress)
Wind power generation: Wind power from three wind mills of aggregate capacity 4.6 MW in Maharashtra, sold to industrial consumers under Open Access
Leasing: Part of land and buildings at Thergaon, Pune leased to Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd under Leave & License Agreement (for manufacturing paper) since the demerger in 2015
Investment activities: Investment activities (stated as a business line; no products named in the report text provided)

currentContext.expansion: Real estate: having successfully completed and handed over 7 residential towers in 'GREENS' (which currently house 722 families), the 8th tower of about 1,65,000 sq. ft. comprising 2, 3 and 4 BHKs is under construction and 'has received good response from the existing residents of GREENS'; it is expected to be completed by the end of next financial year to house 136 families, taking GREENS to over 850 families in over 9,00,000 sq. ft. of carpet area. GREENS is constructed under a partnership arrangement in which the Company holds a 95% stake (AMJ Land Developers), treated as a subsidiary for accounting purposes. The 'GREEN VILLE' project continues to be on hold in view of the disputed applicability of the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, currently pending resolution with Government authorities pursuant to directions of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court; in view of the long delay the Company may have to again approach the High Court. Redevelopment: AMJ Realty Ltd, the wholly owned subsidiary, is actively pursuing proposals for new development as well as redevelopment of existing old housing schemes, and the Company has been awarded two redevelopment projects for which necessary due diligence and documentation are currently in progress; management sees redevelopment as a source of future growth pipeline given the large number of Pune societies, increasing urbanisation, aging infrastructure and higher Permissible Floor Space Index. Wind power: the Company operates three wind power plants of an aggregate capacity of 4.6 MW in Maharashtra (two of the three wind mills situated on forest land leased to the Company), which generated and sold power of 71.82 kwh during the year as against 65.60 kwh in the last year (units reproduced verbatim); no wind capacity addition is disclosed. Leasing: part of the Company's land and buildings at Thergaon, Pune remains leased to Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd under a Leave & License Agreement, renewed for five years with effect from 1st February 2026 on higher rentals by over 175%. NO rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this routed bundle and no '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' block was supplied, so capex_disclosed is correctly empty.

risks.risk: Land-title / Urban Land Ceiling Act dispute over the Thergaon, Pune land
risks.note: The Government contends the Company's land continues to be subject to the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, contrary to the legal opinion received by the Company. The matter is pending with Government authorities after the Bombay High Court ordered time-bound disposal, and the Company may have to again approach the High Court. This land underpins both the leased Thergaon property and (per sibling bundles) the stalled 'GREEN VILLE' project, so an adverse outcome would impair a core asset.

risks.risk: Competition in the Pune residential market
risks.note: 'The sector faces competition particularly from the areas nearby the Company's project' - competing supply is located adjacent to the Company's own development, so it bears on pricing and absorption of the GREENS towers directly.

'Although the demand by and large remains fairly stable, the larger supply and inflation does put pressures at times on demand' - management explicitly flags episodic demand pressure despite broadly stable underlying demand.

risks.risk: Stiff competition for society redevelopment mandates
risks.note: The redevelopment segment, which management positions as the future growth pipeline, 'faces stiff competition from developers offering increasingly higher free area and compensation' - i.e. winning mandates requires giving away more area/compensation, compressing developer economics.

risks.risk: Single-geography concentration - the entire housing business is in and around Pune
risks.note: 'The Company's business comprises of real estate development for housing project in and around Pune' with the wind mills in Maharashtra and the leased property at Thergaon, Pune - a structural geographic concentration, disclosed as fact rather than labelled as a risk.

risks.risk: Execution concentrated in subsidiary/partnership vehicles rather than the listed entity
risks.note: 'The real estate development is carried out through its subsidiaries, namely; AMJ Land Developers, a firm in which the Company holds 95% stake and wholly owned subsidiary Company, AMJ Realty Ltd.' - the listed company's real-estate earnings depend on entities it does not wholly own in one case (95% firm).

risks.risk: Wind assets partly dependent on leased forest land
risks.note: 'Two of these wind mills are situated on the forest land leased out to the Company' - two of the three wind mills (of the aggregate 4.6 MW) sit on leased forest land rather than owned land, creating tenure/renewal dependence.

risks.risk: High Open Access levies on third-party sale of wind power (BACK-FILLED FROM SIBLING BUNDLE)
risks.note: PROVENANCE: this risk is NOT present in the risks_esg routing - its MD&A section truncates immediately before the paragraph. It is back-filled verbatim from the sibling bundles profile.txt / capex_expansion.txt (Directors' Report and Corporate Governance Report routings), which state: 'This generation and sale of wind power is governed by Electricity Regulatory framework under Open Access system which imposes higher levies resulting in hardly any incentive to consumers to source renewable power from generators' and 'These levies tend to reduce the net realization of the Company, which has marginally increased during the year. High Open Access levies tends to discourage sale of such power to third party consumers.'

risks.risk: Risk governance framework in place (mitigant, disclosed as policy only)
risks.note: 'In accordance with the requirements of the Act, the Company has adopted and implemented a Risk Management Policy for identifying risks to the Company, procedures to inform Board members about the risk assessment & minimization procedures, monitoring the risk management plan, etc.' No risk register, no material-risk table and no BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table was supplied in this bundle, so the enumerated risks above are drawn from MD&A narrative rather than a formal risk disclosure.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company's business comprises real estate development for housing projects in and around Pune, wind power generation and investment activities. Real estate development is carried out through its subsidiaries, namely AMJ Land Developers (a firm in which the Company holds 95% stake) and wholly owned subsidiary AMJ Realty Ltd; its flagship is the gated residential project 'GREENS', which currently houses 722 families in 7 residential towers with an 8th tower under construction, while the 'GREEN VILLE' project remains on hold. products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Real estate development (housing):** GREENS - self-contained prestigious gated residential project, Pune (7 towers handed over; 8th tower of 2, 3 and 4 BHK apartments under construction), GREEN VILLE - project currently on hold, Redevelopment of existing old housing schemes (pursued through AMJ Realty Ltd; two redevelopment projects awarded, due diligence and documentation in progress)
- **Wind power generation:** Wind power from three wind mills of aggregate capacity 4.6 MW in Maharashtra, sold to industrial consumers under Open Access
- **Leasing:** Part of land and buildings at Thergaon, Pune leased to Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd under Leave & License Agreement (for manufacturing paper) since the demerger in 2015
- **Investment activities:** Investment activities (stated as a business line; no products named in the report text provided)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Residential housing buyers in and around Pune, Maharashtra (apartments of different sizes for different categories)
- Old housing societies in Pune requiring redevelopment (higher Permissible Floor Space Index, new-age amenities)
- Industrial consumers of wind power in Maharashtra under the Open Access arrangement
- Leave & License lessee of Thergaon, Pune land and buildings (Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Pune has a constantly expanding area of urbanization, necessitating housing development of different sizes of apartments meant for different categories
- Demand by and large remains fairly stable, but larger supply and inflation do put pressures at times on demand
- The sector faces competition, particularly from areas nearby the Company's project
- Pune has many old housing societies with apartments that lack modern amenities and need redevelopment to cater to demand for larger apartments (in view of higher Permissible Floor Space Index) and new-age amenities
- The redevelopment sector faces stiff competition from developers offering increasingly higher free area and compensation
- Management believes redevelopment projects offer significant growth opportunities due to the large number of societies, increasing urbanization, aging infrastructure and demand for modern residential and commercial spaces, considering higher development potential, infrastructure connectivity, lower capital and return on investment
- Rental realisation from the leased Thergaon property steps up materially - the Leave & License agreement was renewed for five years from 1st February 2026 on higher rentals by over 175%
- Overhang on the land at Thergaon: the Government contends the land remains subject to the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, contrary to the legal opinion received by the Company; the matter is pending with Government authorities after the Bombay High Court's order to dispose of it in a time-bound manner and the Company may have to again approach the High Court
- GREENS - the 8th tower is under construction and will house another 136 families in apartments of 2, 3 and 4 BHKs; with this GREENS would house over 850 families in over 9,00,000 sq. ft. of carpet area (against 722 families in 7 residential towers currently)
- Redevelopment proposals are described by management as a potential contributor to 'the Company's future growth pipeline' - no specific projects or values are named in this routed section

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Pursue participation in redevelopment of Pune's old housing societies - management states that strategic participation in redevelopment proposals can contribute to the Company's future growth pipeline and improve its competitive positioning in the residential sector
- Continue the phased build-out of the GREENS gated residential project in Pune - 7 residential towers house 722 families today and the 8th tower is under construction to house another 136 families in 2, 3 and 4 BHK apartments
- Execute real estate development through the group's development vehicles rather than directly - AMJ Land Developers (a firm in which the Company holds a 95% stake) and the wholly owned subsidiary AMJ Realty Ltd
- Continuous monitoring of market trends, government policies and stakeholder expectations as an integral part of the Company's redevelopment strategy
- Retain wind power generation (three wind mills of aggregate 4.6 MW in Maharashtra) and investment activities alongside real estate as the Company's other business lines
- Monetise the owned Thergaon, Pune land and buildings through leasing - the Leave & License Agreement with Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd has been renewed for five years with effect from 1st February 2026 on higher rentals by over 175%
- Stated policy (Note 23, Capital Risk Management): the Company's policy is to maintain an adequate capital base so as to maintain creditor and market confidence and to sustain future development; in order to maintain or adjust the capital structure the Company may adjust the amount of dividends paid to shareholders, return capital to shareholders or issue new shares. Capital is monitored using the gearing ratio (net debt divided by total capital plus net debt), with net debt comprising long-term and short-term borrowings less cash and bank balances and liquid investments, and equity comprising equity share capital and other equity managed as capital. The Company states it does not have any borrowings, hence the Net Debt to Equity Ratio is not applicable to the Company - the gearing ratio is accordingly reported as 'NA'. A dividend is declared annually and is on the AGM agenda for 2025-26 (Ordinary Business item 3: 'To declare a dividend on equity shares of the Company for the year 2025-26'); the per-share rate and rupee amounts appear in this bundle only inside financial-statement note tables (dividends note) and have deliberately not been reproduced here. Board procedure provides that all major decisions of policy, strategic formulations, capital expenditure, new investments and major accounting policies are considered by the committees and/or the Board.
- Sexual harassment (POSH Act, 2013): an Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted to deal with complaints from the Company and other companies in the Pudumjee Group; during the year under review NO complaints relating to discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment, were received, no complaints were pending for resolution for more than ninety days, and no complaints remained unresolved as on 31st March, 2026 (stated nil, not blank)
- Maternity Benefit Act, 1961: 'Your Company is compliant with the statutory provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.'
- Conservation of energy and technology absorption: STATED NOT APPLICABLE - 'As the Company is not engaged in the manufacturing activities, the information related to Conservation of energy, technology absorption is not applicable.' This is a stated absence, not a gap
- Foreign exchange earnings and outgo: 'During the year under review, no Foreign Exchange was earned and used' (stated nil for both earnings and outgo)
- CSR: the Company refers to its Corporate Social Responsibility Policy (the policy URL is cut off at the head of the routed section) and states that other relevant disclosures stipulated under the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014 are given in Annexure-3 - the CSR spend/annexure content itself was not supplied in this bundle
- Whistle Blower Policy / Vigil Mechanism in place, framed to reflect amendments to the Companies Act and to comply with Regulation 22 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on the Company's website
- Governance policies disclosed and published on the website: Risk Management Policy, Remuneration Policy (including criteria for qualifications, positive attributes and independence of Directors), Policy on Related Party Transactions (with the Audit Committee reviewing all RPTs quarterly), Policy on evaluation of performance of Directors and the Board, and the Familiarisation Programme for Independent Directors
- Board evaluation: a meeting of the Independent Directors was held on 03rd February, 2026 at which the performance of the Non-Independent Directors, including the Chairman, and of the Board as a whole was evaluated against pre-defined criteria; the Board evaluated the performance of Independent Directors at its meeting on 03rd February, 2026
- Material changes and commitments: 'There are no adverse material changes or commitments that occurred after 31st March, 2026, which may affect the financial position of the Company or may require disclosure' (stated absence)
- Significant and material orders: 'There is no significant and material order passed by the Regulators or Courts or Tribunals impacting the going concern status and Company's operations in future' (stated absence)
- NOTE ON COVERAGE: no BRSR (Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report) section was supplied in this routed bundle, so there are no quantified ESG targets, emissions/energy/water metrics, or 'material responsible business conduct issues' to report; the items above are the ESG-adjacent disclosures the Directors' Report actually makes

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Real estate: having successfully completed and handed over 7 residential towers in 'GREENS' (which currently house 722 families), the 8th tower of about 1,65,000 sq. ft. comprising 2, 3 and 4 BHKs is under construction and 'has received good response from the existing residents of GREENS'; it is expected to be completed by the end of next financial year to house 136 families, taking GREENS to over 850 families in over 9,00,000 sq. ft. of carpet area. GREENS is constructed under a partnership arrangement in which the Company holds a 95% stake (AMJ Land Developers), treated as a subsidiary for accounting purposes. The 'GREEN VILLE' project continues to be on hold in view of the disputed applicability of the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, currently pending resolution with Government authorities pursuant to directions of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court; in view of the long delay the Company may have to again approach the High Court. Redevelopment: AMJ Realty Ltd, the wholly owned subsidiary, is actively pursuing proposals for new development as well as redevelopment of existing old housing schemes, and the Company has been awarded two redevelopment projects for which necessary due diligence and documentation are currently in progress; management sees redevelopment as a source of future growth pipeline given the large number of Pune societies, increasing urbanisation, aging infrastructure and higher Permissible Floor Space Index. Wind power: the Company operates three wind power plants of an aggregate capacity of 4.6 MW in Maharashtra (two of the three wind mills situated on forest land leased to the Company), which generated and sold power of 71.82 kwh during the year as against 65.60 kwh in the last year (units reproduced verbatim); no wind capacity addition is disclosed. Leasing: part of the Company's land and buildings at Thergaon, Pune remains leased to Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd under a Leave & License Agreement, renewed for five years with effect from 1st February 2026 on higher rentals by over 175%. NO rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this routed bundle and no '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' block was supplied, so capex_disclosed is correctly empty.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established, self-contained gated residential franchise in Pune - 'GREENS' is described as a self-contained prestigious gated residential project, and the 8th tower 'has received good response from the existing residents of GREENS', indicating repeat demand from the existing community
- Owned land bank at Thergaon, Pune generating contracted rental income - the Leave & License Agreement with Pudumjee Paper Products Ltd was recently renewed for five years with effect from 1st February 2026 'on higher rentals by over 175%'
- Debt-free balance sheet posture - 'The Company does not have any borrowings, hence Net Debt to Equity Ratio is not applicable to company' (Note 23, Capital Risk Management; qualitative statement only, no figures taken)
- Development executed through a 95%-held partnership firm (AMJ Land Developers) plus a wholly owned subsidiary (AMJ Realty Ltd), giving the Company control of the development vehicles
- Optionality on Pune society redevelopment - management states redevelopment projects offer significant growth opportunities given the large number of societies, increasing urbanisation, aging infrastructure, higher development potential, infrastructure connectivity and lower capital, and AMJ Realty Ltd has already been awarded two redevelopment projects

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Land-title / Urban Land Ceiling Act dispute over the Thergaon, Pune land — The Government contends the Company's land continues to be subject to the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, contrary to the legal opinion received by the Company. The matter is pending with Government authorities after the Bombay High Court ordered time-bound disposal, and the Company may have to again approach the High Court. This land underpins both the leased Thergaon property and (per sibling bundles) the stalled 'GREEN VILLE' project, so an adverse outcome would impair a core asset.
- Competition in the Pune residential market — 'The sector faces competition particularly from the areas nearby the Company's project' - competing supply is located adjacent to the Company's own development, so it bears on pricing and absorption of the GREENS towers directly.
- Oversupply and inflation pressuring demand — 'Although the demand by and large remains fairly stable, the larger supply and inflation does put pressures at times on demand' - management explicitly flags episodic demand pressure despite broadly stable underlying demand.
- Stiff competition for society redevelopment mandates — The redevelopment segment, which management positions as the future growth pipeline, 'faces stiff competition from developers offering increasingly higher free area and compensation' - i.e. winning mandates requires giving away more area/compensation, compressing developer economics.
- Single-geography concentration - the entire housing business is in and around Pune — 'The Company's business comprises of real estate development for housing project in and around Pune' with the wind mills in Maharashtra and the leased property at Thergaon, Pune - a structural geographic concentration, disclosed as fact rather than labelled as a risk.
- Execution concentrated in subsidiary/partnership vehicles rather than the listed entity — 'The real estate development is carried out through its subsidiaries, namely; AMJ Land Developers, a firm in which the Company holds 95% stake and wholly owned subsidiary Company, AMJ Realty Ltd.' - the listed company's real-estate earnings depend on entities it does not wholly own in one case (95% firm).
- Wind assets partly dependent on leased forest land — 'Two of these wind mills are situated on the forest land leased out to the Company' - two of the three wind mills (of the aggregate 4.6 MW) sit on leased forest land rather than owned land, creating tenure/renewal dependence.
- High Open Access levies on third-party sale of wind power (BACK-FILLED FROM SIBLING BUNDLE) — PROVENANCE: this risk is NOT present in the risks_esg routing - its MD&A section truncates immediately before the paragraph. It is back-filled verbatim from the sibling bundles profile.txt / capex_expansion.txt (Directors' Report and Corporate Governance Report routings), which state: 'This generation and sale of wind power is governed by Electricity Regulatory framework under Open Access system which imposes higher levies resulting in hardly any incentive to consumers to source renewable power from generators' and 'These levies tend to reduce the net realization of the Company, which has marginally increased during the year. High Open Access levies tends to discourage sale of such power to third party consumers.'
- Risk governance framework in place (mitigant, disclosed as policy only) — 'In accordance with the requirements of the Act, the Company has adopted and implemented a Risk Management Policy for identifying risks to the Company, procedures to inform Board members about the risk assessment & minimization procedures, monitoring the risk management plan, etc.' No risk register, no material-risk table and no BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table was supplied in this bundle, so the enumerated risks above are drawn from MD&A narrative rather than a formal risk disclosure.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Pursue participation in redevelopment of Pune's old housing societies - management states that strategic participation in redevelopment proposals can contribute to the Company's future growth pipeline and improve its competitive positioning in the residential sector
- Continue the phased build-out of the GREENS gated residential project in Pune - 7 residential towers house 722 families today and the 8th tower is under construction to house another 136 families in 2, 3 and 4 BHK apartments
- Execute real estate development through the group's development vehicles rather than directly - AMJ Land …
